observation_summary: The method appendFixedWidthPadRight throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when the input string length exceeds the specified width, because it attempts to copy the entire string instead of truncating it to the specified width.
hypothesis: The method incorrectly uses the full length of the input string (strLen) as the end index for the getChars operation, rather than the specified width, causing an out-of-bounds access when the string is longer than the target field width.
prediction: Changing the end index parameter in str.getChars(0, strLen, buffer, size) to str.getChars(0, width, buffer, size) will correctly truncate the string to the desired width and prevent the exception.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows exactly this change: replacing 'strLen' with 'width' in the getChars call. This confirms the logic error in the string truncation algorithm.
reasoning_summary: The defect is an incorrect computational step within the method. The procedure is intended to truncate the string to a fixed width, but it incorrectly uses the full string length as the copy limit. This is a classic algorithmic error in data processing logic, not a missing guard (Checking) or a wrong constant (Assignment/Initialization).
evidence_used: The stack trace shows StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at StrBuilder.java:884.
The fix diff shows the change from str.getChars(0, strLen, buffer, size) to str.getChars(0, width, buffer, size).
The bug report description explicitly identifies the logic error in the getChars call.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix prevents an exception, the root cause is not a missing validation check, but an incorrect implementation of the truncation logic itself.
